title: Relations Overview
description: Understand Prisma relation concepts and how relations map to foreign keys in PostgreSQL.

data.text: Relations in Prisma connect models together. They map to foreign key constraints in PostgreSQL and are defined using the `@relation` attribute on both sides of the relationship.

items: **One-to-one** — Each record in Model A relates to at most one record in Model B
**One-to-many** — One record in Model A relates to many records in Model B
**Many-to-many** — Many records in Model A relate to many records in Model B (implicit or explicit)

data.text: Every relation has two sides: a foreign key field and a relation field. The foreign key holds the actual database link, while the relation field is used in Prisma Client queries.

data.title: Relation Example
data.content: A one-to-many relation between User and Post.

data.title: Important
data.text: Prisma requires both sides of a relation to be defined. Omitting one side will cause a validation error when running `prisma migrate dev`.
